Chapter Summary

Mydei and Phainon talk about things. Phainon talks about crows. In return, Mydei talks about a cruel lord.

CW: Violence, gore, child abuse, etc.

You can skip this chapter if you so choose.

POV shifts in this one as well.

Chapter Notes

Sorry.

If you want to skip this, this is the short version: Phainon got into a fight with bandits at age fourteen. Mydei survived a fire at the age of ten. Phainon explains that a child can not be held responsible for actions forced upon them, or what transpires when things are outside their control.

Mydei sat on his sofa in quiet contemplation.

‘Phainon found out about what Haphaestion did to me.’

‘Phainon literally attacked Haphaestion for it.’

‘And now mother is going to find out what Haphaestion did.’

‘She will know.’

He covered himself with the blanket, hiding under it. Hiding from the world around him.

Everything felt like it would fall apart, but for one thing, ‘Phainon risked everything for me.’

‘Why?’

‘I’m not worth that.’

‘Surely I’m not worth the risk of losing his place here.’

‘He earned his place here.’

But so did Haphaestion.

He passed all the exams.

He even got support from his mother.

But how had Cerydra known about Haphaestion before Phainon discovered it?

How, in all the realms of reason, was it possible that she knew?

Who told her?

Unless she knew about his other acts of stupidity from before.

Still things that his mother didn’t know about. Entirely too many things.

But they made it to Cerydra’s ears.

He worked hard to keep Haphaestion under control while here in Okhema. It’s why Leonnius came along. He was the one most suited to subduing the guy.

Had Perdikkas told her? He wouldn’t blame him if he did. His entire job was to protect Mydei while he attended school here. And the biggest threat

to his safety walked alongside him.

He mustn't mourn Haphaestion.

He must not blame Phainon for his actions.

He must not blame himself.

He must not believe himself a coward.

He gripped his arms around himself tightly.

He must not drown in the darkness.

He heard his apartment door unlock, and he suddenly regretted not using the deadbolt.

He didn't move as the door opened and shut behind whoever entered.

The steps of the intruder were soft, and stopped in front of him. He could see the person’s shoes. Incredibly roughshod boots that could only belong to one person.

His guest knelt in front of him.

“Can I come in?” A soft voice asked.

Mydei shook his head.

“I just wanted to make sure you’re okay.”

He felt a warm hand rest on his head over the top of the blanket.

“You don’t have to say anything,” the voice was calm, but carried traces of worry. “I’ll tell you how I found out only if you want me to. But right now, all I want to do is make sure that you’re okay.”

Mydei stared at the knees in front of him, the only part of the visitor visible from his hiding place. He shook his head again.

“I won't then.” His visitor took a deep breath. “Would you let me hug you?”

Mydei blinked at that, taking a moment to let it sink in.

He nodded, closing his eyes as warm arms embraced him, still not forcing him from under the blanket.

“I’m sorry I acted recklessly.”

Mydei shook his head. “You don’t have to apologize to me. I should be thanking you.”

He felt the warm hands against his back. “I will apologize because I acted without talking to you first.”

“Why.” Mydei asked quietly. “Why would you go to such lengths for me?”

“Because you’re the nicest person I know, and I couldn’t stand to let someone who hurt you like that be near you. I hated how he looked at you, like he owned you.”

“But I did nothing to earn your protection, Phainon.”

“Simply existing is the only reason I needed.” Phainon replied softly.

Mydei adjusted the blanket and considered removing it entirely. “I shouldn’t even be alive.”

“I don’t believe that for a single second.”  Phainon’s voice had a harder and more desperate edge than a few seconds ago.

Mydei threw off the blanket and stared at Phainon. “You don’t get to determine my worth. You don’t get to determine if I should be alive.”

Phainon grabbed Mydei’s hands and held them softly together between them. “Things that you were forced to do as a child, even if it was out of desperation or your hand was forced, can not be your fault.”

Mydei’s eyes widened at that. “But you don’t even know what happened.”

“And you don’t have to tell me if you don’t want to.” Phainon’s response was immediate. “I just want you to be okay and to understand that I’m so happy that you’re part of my life.”

Mydei blinked at that, he felt his heart skip a beat. “You-”

Phainon smiled softly, and wiped away a tear Mydei hadn’t noticed he had shed. “If you want, I can tell you about myself. I can tell you why I made that deal with Miss Cerydra.”

Mydei hung his head, giving it a quick shake. “I don’t need to know.”

“Are you sure? It involves cows.” Phainon laughed as he said the words. “I promise, it’s a funny story.”

Mydei looked at Phainon and saw the incredibly serious expression he had. “What?” Mydei half laughed when he asked. “What do cows have to do with anything?” It was entirely too difficult to keep a straight face with the way Phainon was looking at him.

“Yeah. Cows!” He smiled. “Do you wanna know?” He teased.

“You might as well.” Mydei laughed.

Phainon looked so pleased at Mydei’s change in mood.

“You’re such a puppy.” Mydei laughed lightly.

“And you’re a cat.” Phainon responded in kind, and hesitantly carded a hand through Mydei’s hair. He didn’t expect Mydei to lean into his hand.

“Now tell me, would you?” He closed his eyes and really did lean into Phainon’s hand. Somehow Phainon broke through all his defenses and they had become so close.

Phainon barked out a laugh, which startled Mydei. “Seriously, just like a cat!” He smiled. “So, I was fourteen-”

Late one night at his family’s farm, Phainon was woken by an odd sound.

A sound that was distinctly different from the buzz of cicadas and croaking

of frogs.

It was a sound that made him sit up straight; Snowy was barking. He could

tell something was wrong. His parents had long since fallen asleep.

He climbed out of bed and snuck out the front door and headed to the barn.

That’s the direction Snowy’s barking was coming from.

He heard the yelling the closer he got to the barn. Yelling and the distinct

sounds of their cows in distress.

He started to run when a cow squealed and Snowy yelped.

Lucky that the moon was full, he approached the barn and saw what was happening. He saw one of the bandits (he immediately assumed they were

bandits) had kicked Snowy.

He acted entirely on impulse. He ran up to the guy and decked him in the

jaw.

The guy had screamed some obscenity, alerting the rest of the bandits to

Phainon’s existence.

“What are you doing here? Show yourselves!”

Three more men appeared.

“State your intentions!” Phainon demanded.

The bandits laughed.

“What are you going to do about it, kid?”

“I’ll make it so you can’t walk!”

The bandits laughed at the threat.

“You don’t believe me, do you?” Threw himself at another bandit, throwing

him, a crack echoed as he hit the ground.

The bandit cried out in pain.

The remaining two bandits shouted something as one ran away and the

other threatened to burn down the barn.

Phainon rushed the one with the torch, screaming all the while. He drenched the torch away and threw it into the trough next to the barn,

extinguishing it.

But Phainon saw red.

The man whose wrist he held yelped at the strength of that grip. He didn't

expect Phainon to be able to lift him so easily, let alone throw him.

The bandit was screaming as he got thrown through the side of the barn, the

amusing squelch of the man landing in the slop on the other side of the wall

made Phainon smile.

They picked the wrong farm to mess with.

They dared to hurt the dog, and they were trying to do something with their

precious cows. It was unacceptable.

Phainon saw the first bandit try to rush him, and Phainon grabbed the pitchfork that was set aside the barn and slashed at the bandit, drawing

blood and making the man scream in pain.

The guy who landed in the slop had recovered and was going to try to either

attack Phainon or run, but Phainon caught him before he could do anything.

The unfortunate thing was that the tool he was holding found itself lodged in the bandits ribcage. The blood flowed down the handle of the pitchfork,

covering Phainon's hands in blood.

He shoved the ban downwards, pinning him to the ground with the

pitchfork.

The rage blinded him. He didn't remember what happened, but he did remember that he was covered in blood but the dog and the cows were

okay. He was okay.

The other guys, not so much.

Phainon was praised for defending his family’s farm, but scolded and punished for taking two lives that night. One man was run through with the

pitchfork, and the other was the one whose skull had cracked open when

Phainon threw him to the ground.

His punishment didn't match the crime he committed.

But he was punished, even if he was celebrated for protecting his home.

He decided that he would focus on trying to leave his hometown.

As much as he loved being surrounded by the wheat fields, he knew that

those two men's lives would follow him, more so in the land they were

buried than if he were to leave.

The best option was studying and getting into a good school.

At some point, Miss Cerydra stopped by the village, but he hadn't found out

about it until after his acceptance to the school in Okhema.

Cerydra guaranteed his family a scholarship if he kept himself from engaging in more violent pastimes. He would have to promise to not hurt

anyone beyond what was reasonable at the time.

Take no lives.

But if someone crosses the line; if someone requires justice, and only if- he

is allowed to take action.

Haphaestion crossed that line.

Mydei stared at Phainon. “What about that was funny to you?” The entire story was bizarre, and ended up with Phainon literally killing two guys.

Phainon shrugged. “The guy landing in the slop was funny.”

Mydei squinted at the dumbass in front of him. “But you still killed him.”

“Not on purpose?” He turned his head away, and looked sideways at Mydei. “His friend did kick the dog and he did threaten my family's livelihood.”

“Why are you smiling? That's insane!”

Phainon laughed. “I was a child. I was a child faced with a difficult situation. I acted without thinking, and I saved more lives than I took.” His tone became somber. “What I mean to demonstrate by telling you this is that we both seemed to face situations that we couldn't actually control. Neither of us had the wherewithal to act differently.” He sighed, not looking directly at Mydei. “So whatever happened in your childhood; whatever you had to do because of your father, you are not guilty for. The actions taken by a child are just that. Acting in the confines of a world we didn't yet grasp. The same consequences that haunt us are consequences that belong to the people who forced our hands.” Another deep sigh. “Whatever we regret, whatever we carry with us- those are punishment enough for whatever we were forced to do.” His tone was filled with melancholy. “We can't change the past. Our pasts are part of who we are. Good and bad experiences alike. While we don't believe our actions to be justified, they also are not ours to judge.”

Mydei stared at him, absolute disbelief written all over his face.

He swallowed hard. “I set my house on fire.” Mydei looked to the side. “I think I did, at least.”

Phainon slowly turned to look at Mydei. “You think? As in you don't remember?”

“I remember a lot of it, but not how the fire started.” Mydei sighed. “My father had beaten my mother bloody, her legs would never work again.”

“How old were you?”

Mydei paused and took a deep breath. “I was ten.”

The house was massive.

The sounds of his mother's screams would have women the neighbors if

they had had any.

All the attendants were forced into silence. They would not be allowed to speak of this, or else they would also face the lord's wrath. Completely cold.

Completely mirthless.

Mydei was forced to remain seated at the table, dinner growing cold as the

lord proceeded to break his mother's legs.

Her screams burned Mydei's soul.

He screamed for his father to stop.

This earned him a knife to his skin, pressed hard and drawing blood.

His mother screamed for him to stop hurting their child.

The lord did not stop his vicious attack against the two who he was

supposed to treasure.

Mydei had to watch as his father stuck something into the fireplace, and the

scent of hot iron filled the room.

Mydei watched as his father approached him with the poker.

Mydei screamed as the red hot poker touched right under his eye. Not hard

enough to melt the flesh, but enough to leave a mark. Enough to make the

message stick.

Mydei watched as the lord turned to his mother, and held the hot metal to

her legs, searing through her clothes and into her skin.

He had to act.

His mother was going to be hurt more.

The lord was relentless in his rage that night.

Mydei cried as he seized the man by his jacket. “Stop hurting her! Stop it!”

He was thrown to the floor with a simple smack of his father’s hand. “You

would do well to learn your place, boy.” A cold voice, filled with so much

disgust and hatred that it would forever echo in the boy's mind.

At some point, the candelabras on the table fell.

At some point, the fire spread.

He tried to drag his mother from the fire.

A ten-year-old boy, without the help of the staff, did his best to drag his

mother away from the fire.

The only person who helped him was Krateros, but that was after he had

seen the smoke. After the damage had been done.

His mother couldn't talk for years.

His father forced him into an exile so young. Left him with nothing, not

even shoes, at the shores of Styxia. Hoping that the boy would die.

He had paid off the local officials to not aid the boy in any way.

The boy learned the language of the land out of necessity. Only a few families were willing to help him. One of them had two daughters, one of

whom was born without the use of her legs.

That family defended and hid Mydei when the guards came after him.

They were the ones who got him off the island.

Polyxia and Castorice very likely didn't remember him, he was so different

now.

He had made himself stronger, he worked hard to become someone who his

father wouldn't dare threaten.

And he eventually covered his scars with red ink. Marking himself with his

sin of starting that fire. Forever branding himself for the weight of his

mother's suffering.

Mydei didn't cry as he recounted the story, and he didn't look up at Phainon either.

Phainon was crying, the sound of it made Mydei look up.

“I carry that sin with me.” He buried his face in his hands.

“You can't blame yourself for the actions of your father.” Phainon placed his hand on Mydei’s face. “You were ten. You were ten and he did something unforgivable. You acted the way any child would have.” His blue eyes filled with compassion beyond words. “I guarantee your mother is proud of you for surviving and helping her survive.”

Mydei’s eyes teared up at that. He nodded, crying freely.

He felt that weight lift, and the scars didn’t burn for once.

Phainon helped him carry the truth that he never even told his closest friends.

Chapter End Notes

dear Godzilla I have been wanting to explain Phainon's throwing a kid through a barn since I first mentioned it. Mydei's backstory needed an explanation because of how Phainon's story affected him.

I'm so sorry I did this to my boys. Yes, Mydei has scars from all sorts of shit on his body, the worst of which he managed to cover with tattoos. He chose that for himself as a means of repenting. He didn't explain them to his mother, either.

chapters.title: Chapter 25: Sounds Like a Plan to Me
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

Mydei makes breakfast.

110% fluff, I promise.

Chapter Notes

This chapter accidentally got really long, I'm sorry.

Mydei slept in.

He had let Phainon stay the night.

They didn’t do much beyond watch a movie or two, they fell asleep on the sofa, Phainon insisted on Mydei stretching out, legs over his lap.

Mydei felt safe and comfortable, so it was fine. He had insisted on Phainon borrowing some extra pajamas, and on making them dinner. He laughed when Phainon brought out the quilt again, and laughed harder when he saw the plush chimera. He also made sure to get an outfit ready for Phainon to wear tomorrow. No matter how Phainon showed up to class the next day, it would imply he spent the night at his place anyway. Yeah, his friends knew that nothing would happen, hell, he had even texted Ptolemy and Perdikkas about it and they seemed to get it.

‘Oh the guy I like decided to come over and make sure I wasn’t wallowing in self hate again but he also told me about the time he killed two guys and I guess we bonded over that,’ was something that he definitely took a while to parse out the phrasing for.

They all understood. Even the girls understood.

Mydei got Phainon to promise to not tell Polyxia and Castorice about the part they played in Mydei’s childhood. Phainon didn’t even hesitate to make that promise.

They fell asleep while watching the absurd “Bartholos the Space Pirate” series, Mydei’s TV turned itself off after the show paused to ask if they were still watching and the screen remained idle too long because no, they had fallen asleep.

Mydei slept in, but so did Phainon.

Apparently Ptolemy promised to take notes for them both because the only class that morning was Anaxa’s.

Cipher had messaged him as well, saying that for once, Anaxa wouldn’t penalize them for not being in attendance, as Cerydra had explained their odd situation. Cipher also reminded him that Polyxia and Castorice were recording their vocals today, and Cipher would record the new drum portion soon.

Mydei: I have some lyrics to change because of what’s happened.

Mydei: The rhythm and tune will be the same.

Mydei: I’ll get that done asap and let the three of you know when it’s done.

Cipher: Righty-o, my dude.

Mydei was thankful that she was patient right now.

He knew that the twins would also understand.

Things had changed a little, after all.

He went to take a shower and wash his face.

Phainon knocked on the door while he was in the shower.

“Yeah?” Mydei called out.

“I’m not gonna come in, but I want to say thank you for yesterday.”

Mydei laughed and turned the shower off, he had already finished anyway. He wrapped the towel around himself and dried his hair with another, and left the bathroom like that.

Mydei glared at Phainon who looked absolutely shocked at Mydei’s state of dress. “Take a shower.” He went to his room and closed the door to get dressed.

“Okay,” he heard Phainon respond. He heard the bathroom door shut and then open again almost immediately, followed by a knock on his bedroom door. “Where are the towels?”

Mydei couldn’t help but laugh at that. “Give me a second and I’ll show you.” He pulled his pants on and, towel still on his head, exited his bedroom and made his way to help Phainon. “I shouldn’t have assumed you knew where they were, sorry.” He moved past Phainon to open the linen cabinet and pull out two towels. “You can put them in the hamper when you’re done, I’ve got a set of clothes for you to wear, too.” He moved past Phainon again, his heart suddenly racing. “I’ll bring them over before you shower.” The words spilled from his mouth rapidly. When he returned to the bathroom with the clothes, Phainon was already half-undressed. “I-UH.” And Mydei hastily set the clothes down before leaving and closing the door. “D-don’t change with the door open!” He felt his face burn with the realization that the guy he really, really liked was in the other room, soon to be naked, and he also looked like that under his clothes. He reiterated into his room and closed the door, attempting to not slam it, behind him before leaning against said door and trying to calm down.

‘Who blessed that man with that body?’ He buried his face in his hands and let out a very quiet scream. ‘He’s so hot!? What the fuck!?’ This was a spiral he let himself indulge in for a very brief moment, and shelved the sight in a place where he could easily access it in his brain. He managed to

finish getting dressed without further issue, having to remind himself that he hadn’t told Phainon how he felt yet, and that he would not think about such indecent things before that.

‘After, sure, if Phainon likes me too, but not right now. Nope. NOPE. DO NOT THINK ABOUT THAT RIGHT NOW.’

He slapped himself in the face a few times and composed himself enough to whip up a late breakfast. Simple by his standards. Crepes, strawberries, a chocolate mousse, and chocolate drizzle- a totally normal thing to make, right?

He also made strawberry lemonade. Granted, he only added sliced strawberries to the lemonade he had made earlier that week, but that isn’t the point.

The point was that Phainon walked in on a gorgeous breakfast that he was not expecting whatsoever.

“What’s all this?” He laughed, fiddling with the collar of the shirt that Mydei lent him.

‘Holy fuck he’s wearing my clothes.’ Mydei, for whatever reason, hadn’t considered the effect that this would have on his heart. “It’s breakfast.”

“I can tell that much, I think. Isn’t this a dessert?” Phainon sat down obediently at the table.

“I’m about to fry some bacon, do you want any?” Mydei hadn’t planned on it, but he needed to calm the fuck down or his heart may just explode.

“Sure, bacon’s tasty.” He heard Phainon begin to eat, he ate quietly and didn’t speak, just seemed to enjoy the food.

When Mydei arrived at the table with a plate of hot bacon, Phainon seemed giddy. “What’s that face for?”

“It’s because I’ve never had a breakfast this good! And it’s something you made!” He picked up a piece of bacon and quickly devoured it. “Where did

you learn to cook?”

“I taught myself.” Mydei said, sitting down across from Phainon so he could start eating. “I wanted to be able to make food for my mom.” He explained, a nostalgic tone in his voice. “I wanted to be able to cook the foods we enjoyed before everything went to shit.” He laughed and ate more of his crepe. “We used to have a small beehive so we would always have fresh honey.” The memory was warm and happy. I was still very little at the time, so my memory of it all isn’t perfect, but my time in Styxia and seeing how much my mother suffered drove me to learn how to cook. I realized that food is the easiest way to speak to some people.” He sighed and took a sip of lemonade. “My mother always loves when I make her food, and I want to get better at it for her.”

“Not for yourself?”

Mydei laughed at that. “I guess I always put her first because of all that happened.”

Phainon ate another piece of bacon. “I think you need to focus on doing things for yourself.” He smiled. “If you work towards other people’s happiness, you’re bound to lose sight of yourself in the process.”

Mydei looked at Phainon, took in that smile, and returned it with a soft smile of his own. “I’m still figuring out what I can do for myself where I won’t feel too selfish.” He finished his crepe and bacon. “It’s hard, when you’ve lived a life like mine.”

“That’s fair.” Phainon laughed lightly. “We all have our own shit, and both of us went through really, really bad shit.” He had more lemonade. “But that’s why it’s good to have someone to remind you that it’s just shit. Shit can be cleaned up.”

Mydei couldn’t help but laugh at that. “Says a guy who threw a guy through a wall into a pile of shit!”

“Right? Now you see why it’s a funny story.”

Mydei laughed at that, too. “I guess it is, when you put it that way.”

“Yeah, all things considered, I just remind myself that yesterday is yesterday's problem, today is my problem, and tomorrow is tomorrow’s problem.” The smile on his face was one befitting a toddler who just discovered paint and would conquer the world in messy handprints.

“You really are just like a puppy.” Mydei smiled back at him. “You say some of the craziest shit and you say it so damn proudly that I can’t help but be impressed.”

“Oh, so I impress you now?” Phainon wiggled his eyebrows in an attempt to pull another laugh out of Mydei.

And it worked. “Why, is it odd that I find you impressively weird?”

“Ah, but at least you found me!” Phainon locked eyes with Mydei. “Weird or not, you still found me!”

Mydei’s heart skipped, and he immediately stood up to gather the dishes. “You’re hard to miss.” He smiled as he turned away from Phainon. ‘Too damn perfect to ignore.’

“Ah, but I am good at dodging!”

Mydei coughed out a laugh at that one, and started to wash up after himself. “You’re speaking nonsense!”

“The only cents I make are part of my scholarship, so… at least two dollars. I’m speaking with at least two dollars in my wallet.” Phainon failed at completely hiding his laugh from his terrible joke.

“How many of those jokes do you have?”

“Enough of them to embarrass you for all of time,” Phainon stood next to Mydei now. “Want me to help?”

Mydei cursed how fast his heart beat at that. ‘What did he say?’ He made sure to breathe and not drop the plate in his hand. “You can dry them if you

want.” He gestured at the drawer that contained the dish towels, “But otherwise, not really.”

“One other question first,” Phainon waited until Mydei looked at him.

“Yes?”

“Can I hug you?” The look on his face was dead serious.

“Maybe after the dishes are dry and if I’m feeling up for it.” Mydei returned to focusing on the dishes, hoping that he wasn’t visibly blushing at that. ‘Of course you can hug me whenever you want.’ His heart hammered, and he really struggled at keeping his composure. “So, Aedes Elysiae,” Mydei started softly.

“Yeah?” Phainon started drying things. “What about it?”

“What’s it like?” Mydei really wanted to know.

“It’s hard to describe, honestly.” Phainon hummed a little song as he worked. “It’s by the ocean, and the dock there is in shambles. Cyrene and I wanted to try to build a boat once and we never succeeded in making it float.” He laughed. “Cyrene is the only other person my- our age who lives there if I haven’t told you yet.” He stared at the plate in his hand for a moment. “There is wheat as far as the eye can see, dirt roads that with fences of stone and wood wind through houses made of wood, stone, and clay. The roofs are made with thatch, and need to be redone every now and then or else they rot.” He smiled. “There’s an unfortunately damaged statue of Oronyx right by the building that we used for a school. Pythias, my teacher, worked hard to keep it clean despite the kids dragging dirt in all the time. There are wind chimes everywhere, all sorts of tones, too. You could hear a symphony from them in the right weather.” He laughed lightly. “And, you’ll laugh, but there are also fairies who live there. They have a hideaway under a tree in the forest. Cyrene and I discovered them purely by chance when we were very young.”

“Really?” Mydei paused to look at Phainon. “You’re telling me, little critters with wings?”

Phainon turned to Mydei and softly laughed, “They’re more like weird rabbits with big fluffy tails. There are illustrations of them in the book Cyrene gifted me before I came here.”

“The blue one, right?”

“Yeah. It’s called As I’ve Written, and the author’s name is unknown, just a drawing of an illustration of a peach enveloped in flowers where the name should be. It’s a strange book, but the stories are beyond fascinating.”

“Yeah? I’d like to see it sometime.” Mydei had seen it before, but he didn’t page through it. He had held it, and provided Phainon with a bookmark, which is STILL tucked in the pages last he saw. “I hope you found a suitable bookmark since you lost yours before school started.” Mydei said before he realized the words betraying his second time meeting Phainon.

“Hm?” Phainon looked at him while holding the pan he used for the crepes. “How did you know I lost my bookmark?”

“Lucky guess. You seem like the kind of guy who’d lose that sort of thing if you weren’t careful.” Mydei’s cover was very, very flimsy, but he was as nonchalant as possible with it.

“Honestly, the original one may have just flown away.”

“Bookmarks can fly?”

“This one was a golden feather. I don’t even know where it came from originally, I just know that Cyrene found it and gave it to me with the book.” He laughed some more. “I don’t know how I managed to keep it in the book as long as I did, to be completely honest.” He set the pan aside, as it was definitely dry now. “I ended up with a piece of paper that I don’t remember where it came from either as my current bookmark.”

“Oh?” Mydei did his best to not bring up that it was a letter that his mom had written to Cerydra.

“Yeah, I unfortunately spilled water on it before I could actually translate it, but it was definitely Kremnoan. The ink ran so badly, I had to iron the paper before I could put it back in my book so I didn’t damage the book!”

Mydei didn’t hold back the laugh. “So you have some random letter from someone you don’t know as a bookmark?” He almost snorted while laughing at that. “That’s so strange, why would you do that?”

“Honestly, I thought an angel may have given it to me,” Phainon’s smile was wide. “So I just hung on to it.”

“Angels now?” Mydei clearly remembered Phainon asking him if he were an angel that day. “You’re going with ‘And Angel Ate My Homework’ as your honest answer?”

“If it gets me out of trouble, why not?” Phainon shrugged and grabbed the last dish that he needed to dry. “Besides, I’m pretty sure that I wasn’t dreaming.”

Mydei didn’t turn up to look at Phainon. He was hoping that Phainon would have completely forgotten that interaction, considering he had been awake for maybe two whole minutes of it- barely awake in fact! “That’s just silly.” Mydei grabbed a different towel and dried his hands.

“Maybe.” Phainon turned wholly towards Mydei. “So, can I give you a hug now?”

“What?”

“You said I could ask again after the dishes were clean if I could hug you?”

Mydei had honestly forgotten. He was getting more of Phainon than his heart could handle platonically at the moment that it completely slipped his mind.

“Is that a no?”

“It isn’t a no.” Mydei paused. “Why do you want to hug me anyways?” He asked. ‘Please hug me,’ he screamed internally. ‘I would like that very

much, actually.’ But he couldn’t find it in him to actually speak those thoughts out loud.

Phainon wrapped his arms around Mydei’s shoulders from behind. “I just want to, that’s all.”

Mydei bristled at the sudden nature of it and scoffed. “You are so much like a dog it’s crazy.”

“And you’re still like a cat!” Phainon’s voice was right next to his ear.

Mydei thought his heart would legitimately explode from the contact, let alone Phainon’s breath on his neck. “How am I like a cat? That’s absurd!” He wanted so badly to lean into that hug and melt in that warmth, but he did his best to remain calm and not do that.

“Because you’re practically purring right now?”

Mydei froze at that comment. “I’m what.”

Phainon’’s laugh tickled his neck. “Purring, but like, not really. It’s hard to describe. But yeah, purring works for what I’m trying to say.”

“Kremnoan may be lacking words, but surely you have words for what you think I am doing.”

Phainon spoke in that language of his, softly and calmly, swaying lightly with Mydei in his arms. “The word exists in that language, but not in Okheman.” He sighed. “It’s truly unfortunate."

“One of these days you’re going to teach me that language even if I have to fight you to get it out of you.”

Phainon laughed at that. “Sounds like a plan to me.”

Chapter End Notes

Chapter Notes

One month later:

When Mydei handed Phainon the flashdrive, the guy looked so confused. And Mydei had been too embarrassed to say anything when he gave it to him.

And now he was anxious.

Mydei impatiently waited for Phainon’s response.

He had finally handed over the flash drive with the song on it.

He was nervous.

He sat at the cafe with Perdikkas, who was there mainly to make sure he didn’t self-destruct.

Actually their entire friend group knew that he was waiting very, very impatiently.

He ate whatever Perdikkas had set in front of him. It was sweet and tasted amazing, but he was too busy being impatient, tapping his foot on the

ground and his fingers on the table.

“Can you at least look at the food you’re eating?” Perdikkas asked, leaning back in his seat. “You know that he’s gonna hear it, and you probably even know what his reaction is gonna be.” He shoved a glass towards Mydei. “You shouldn’t worry yourself sick over it, but you should pay attention to what I’m putting in front of you.”

“It’s been hours.” Mydei kept checking his phone. “Why has it been hours?”

“Because Phainon had, like, two classes to go to so he was probably very preoccupied,” his friend supplied the answer that made the most sense. “You really need to relax, Dei.”

Mydei finally looked at the plate in front of him and furrowed his brow. “You’ve been feeding me cookies?

“I very much have been.” Perdikkas laughed at that comment. “The owner of this place has been very entertained by the two of you, it seems. She even gave you that shake for free when she realized that you’re finally telling Phainon how you feel.”

“Wait, what?” Mydei looked at Perdikkas in disbelief. “Why would- Has it been- What?”

“Oh, she’s been rooting for you since you introduced us to him properly. She apparently saw the whole exchange between the two of you that day and found it cute.” He said it so painfully calmly before consuming more of his own milkshake.

Mydei swallowed hard. “What?” his voice cracked. ‘WHAT?’ He was screaming inside his own head.

“Basically everyone has been on the edge of their seats over you two.” Casually sliding over his phone to show Mydei that there was actually a whole fanpage dedicated to the pair online.

“What the fuck?” Mydei squeaked. He scrolled through the page, looking at the absurd posts and the fact that there were photos that people had taken of the two of them, captioned with things like ‘How are they NOT a thing yet?’, ‘There’s no way it’s just tutoring.’ and ‘Can you imagine how cute their kids would be?’

Mydei didn’t even want to consider the implications of that last comment, but the photo with it was of the two of them at the diner a little over a month ago captioned ‘The lion actually ordered puppy food without asking holy shit. THIS IS NOT A DRILL. AND THEY DRANK FROM THE SAME GLASS!!!!!’

He felt slightly violated by the nature of the page’s existence, but couldn’t stop looking at the photos. Some were very clear and showed Mydei smiling or laughing, and how Phainon looked at him with his goofy grin. He remembered so many of these things, and it was weird to see it from an outsider’s perspective.

It was a very strange thing to look at.

His phone buzzed.

He rushed to look at it.

Phainon: Ro tsm hkgr ikeugo wisr grs, eh? The same goes for you.

Mydei stood up quickly, almost knocking over the chair. His heart really couldn’t take it.

Mydei: Good.

‘Good. You typed ‘good’ that’s a shit way to react to that. Great job, Mydei.’

Phainon: You wrote a whole song for me?

Phainon: You could have just asked me out directly.

Phainon: Unless, of course, you’re too shy.

Mydei hurried out of the cafe as he hit the call button.

“Hey,” Phainon’s voice was more casual than he expected. “How are you doing?”

“Will you go out with me?” Mydei wanted to say hello, but the question happened first.

“Only if you ask me in person.” Phainon’s tone was teasing.

“Where the fuck are you so I can do that then?”

“Heading out from my dorm, you?”

“I just- I’m at the cafe.” Mydei was so flustered. “I’m actually outside the cafe,” he corrected himself.

“Meet me at the park across the street, okay?”

“Y-yeah.” Mydei nodded as if Phainon could see the reaction. “Heading there now.”

“Hang up so you don’t get hit by a car,” the laugh from the other end of the phone was everything.

“Fine.” Mydei didn’t hang up while he made his way over to the park. “The lights at these corners are too damn long,” he muttered under his breath as he waited for the walk signal to light up. When it did, he practically ran to the park. He still hadn't hung up on Phainon, who was likely subjected to the sounds of shuffling fabric as he ran.

When he saw Phainon, he was holding his phone to his ear, smiling, and pointed to his phone like Mydei should do the same. So he did.

“You know,” Phainon spoke, standing still and looking at Mydei from across the lawn. “I’ve been waiting for this call for a while now.”

“Really now?”

“Yeah.” He heard the laugh through the phone, but not from where he stood. “I even told you I would wait for however long it took.”

Mydei almost dropped his phone as he hung up. He rushed towards Phainon, almost tackling him with a hug that was immediately returned, he buried his face in Phainon’s chest.

“Will you go out with me?” He mumbled into the fabric of Phainon’s shirt, causing the guy to laugh.

“Of course I will.” Phainon pried Mydei off of him just enough to look Mydei in the eye.

Mydei took that chance to put his hands on Phainon’s face to pull him into a kiss- one he had been wanting for so long that it was almost painful- and loved the feeling of it being returned with just as much longing.

“I love you, Mydei.” Phainon whispered.

Mydei felt the tears well in his eyes.

“I love you too, Phainon,” and proceeded to bury his face in Phainon’s shirt again, laughing as he did so, the tears fell freely. “I love you so much. Stay with me, please.”

Phainon hugged Mydei tighter.

“I will, don’t worry.” Phainon was also crying, according to the tears he felt on his neck. “I’ll always be here.”
